speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Since then, the work of PUB has continued to evolve.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Third, PUB continues to leverage technology to improve service quality.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As announced in January this year, PUB will roll out some 300,000 smart water meters in homes and commercial and industrial buildings by 2023.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Lastly, to complement PUB's efforts in ensuring the security of our water supply, we will also need building owners and managers to do their part to keep our water supply system secure, by protecting their water tanks against unauthorised access.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Against the backdrop of these developments, it is necessary to update the Public Utilities Act in four key areas to ensure that it remains effective and relevant.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The first group of amendments will expressly confer new coastal protection functions on PUB and legislate the new Coastal and Flood Protection Fund.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: PUB is currently the national authority for drainage and inland flood protection.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Given the synergy in tackling inland flooding and coastal inundation risks together in a holistic manner, the Government has tasked PUB to be the national Coastal Protection Agency.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: PUB will work with agencies and other stakeholders to enhance our coastline defences and coordinate policies to facilitate decisions on land use, development and activities to safeguard Singapore against rising sea levels.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will use this fund prudently to implement coastal protection measures, which could include sea walls, tidal gates and pumping stations.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These are all being studied, and may need to be deployed together to prevent flooding.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Fund will also be used to help PUB expand Singapore’s drainage infrastructure to cope with more intense rainfall arising from climate change.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Coastal and Flood Protection Fund signals the Government’s resolve in tackling long-term existential challenges such as climate change.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Given the significant outlay, we will need a combination of funding methods to finance our adaptation measures.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Coastal and Flood Protection Fund will be just one source of funding.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will study this closely and assess what other appropriate funding sources should be used.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These sources may include budgets of Ministries, borrowing and tapping on Past Reserves where land reclamation is involved.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Prime Minister also said in his National Day Rally speech, that everything else must bend at the knees to safeguard the existence of our island nation.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Planning and investing long-term for coastal defences and national flood protection will be critical to ensure that Singapore has adequate resources to meet this challenge.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The second group of amendments will provide for legislative safeguards over our water infrastructure, especially water supply plants.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As the House is aware, we have been diversifying our water sources by building up four national taps over the decades.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The intent is to safeguard our water security.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As we build up our desalination and NEWater capacity, PUB has partnered the private sector to design, build, own and operate our DBOO, some of our desalination and NEWater plants.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This DBOO model allows PUB to tap on the expertise and resources of the private sector to deliver water solutions most cost-effectively.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: By the end of this year, PUB will have six out of 10 desalination and NEWater plants under the DBOO model.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The remaining four plants are owned and operated by PUB.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For the DBOO plants, PUB has put in place robust contractual safeguards to ensure water security.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For example, concession companies that own and operate DBOO plants are obliged to seek PUB’s approval when there is a change in control.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Under the contractual terms, PUB can terminate the contracts and buy over the plants, or in some cases, step in to operate the plants, should the need arise.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We have successfully executed some of these contractual remedies in the past to ensure our water security.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Water security is critical to Singapore’s national security.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: While we have already strong contractual safeguards, given that water security is an existential issue to Singapore, we need to always look for ways to strengthen safeguards over our water infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We have reviewed the regulatory regimes of other critical infrastructure, such as electricity and telecommunications, and concluded that it would be prudent to adopt similar legislative safeguards that are already in place in these sectors.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Taking reference from these other legislation, the Bill will strengthen PUB's oversight of the concession companies.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These concession companies, as well as any underlying trusts or business trusts that may be set up to hold the plant assets, will be designated by PUB and be subject to additional oversight mechanisms under the Bill.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Broadly, under clause 8, all designated parties will be subject to three types of oversight controls.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is to ensure that control of DBOO plants rests with individuals or groups whose interests are aligned with the long-term interests of Singapore’s water security and the public interest.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For example, we may need to ensure that there is sufficient diversity in the ownership and operation of DBOO plants in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This will reduce the risk to Singapore’s water security from having mega conglomerates monopolising our critical infrastructure but then unexpectedly collapsing.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Given the strategic role that DBOO plants play in Singapore’s water security, PUB must maintain oversight of controllers who directly or indirectly control substantial equity interest and/or voting power in these designated parties.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Second, these designated parties cannot be dissolved, terminated or wound up voluntarily without PUB’s consent.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The dissolution, termination or winding up of these designated parties will adversely affect our water security.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: If there are court proceedings for the dissolution, termination or winding up of these designated parties, PUB will be a party to such proceedings, and the court must consider representations made by PUB in such proceedings.This ensures that the court does not make any decision without having considered water security considerations.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In addition, the creditors of these designated parties cannot enforce security over the property of such parties, or enforce any court order against such parties, without giving prior notice to PUB.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: An SAO is an order of the Minister directing the takeover of control of the affairs, business and property of a designated party by another person, so as to ensure the continued operations of the DBOO plant for the public interest.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As far as possible, PUB will continue to rely on existing contractual safeguards where appropriate, which have served PUB well thus far.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: But as I mentioned earlier, when it comes to water security, we take no chances.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The third group of amendments relate to smart water meters.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This will allow PUB to leverage digital technologies to encourage behavioural change towards water conservation, optimise water demand management, and achieve greater operational efficiencies.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The updated provisions would empower PUB to: first, install smart water meters, including ancillary equipment; second, enter premises at reasonable hours or at such other time as may be agreed with the owner or occupier of the premise to carry out inspection or works on smart water meters; third, direct the owner to remove any object that hinders or obstructs access to a smart water meter; and fourth, take action against any person who interferes, interrupts or obstructs with the operation of a smart water meter supplied by PUB.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In addition, the amendments specify the circumstances under which a person would be presumed to have tampered with a smart water meter and thus committed an offence.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The last group of amendments relate to water tank security.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: While PUB had made great efforts to protect its water infrastructure and ensure that potable water supplied to consumers is safe and fit for drinking, building owners and managing agents also have a part to play in ensuring our water remains safe for drinking.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For example, they need to take the necessary steps to prevent unauthorised access to the water tanks in their buildings, as these intrusions may disrupt or contaminate the water supply to consumers.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Currently, a lapse in water tank security, such as failing to lock the water tank access door, is already an offence under the Public Utilities (Water Supply) Regulations.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The offence carries a maximum penalty of $10,000, or imprisonment of up to 12 months, or both.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: PUB can offer to compound the offence by collecting a sum not exceeding $3,000.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is in line with the maximum penalty amount for causing contamination to the water supply by PUB, or interfering with or disrupting PUB’s water supply.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In addition, the maximum composition sum for such offences will also be increased from $3,000 to $10,000.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The increased penalties will serve to remind building owners and management teams to take water tank security seriously.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The vast majority of the building owners and management teams are diligent in ensuring water tank security and need not be concerned by the change.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As PUB takes on a new role to defend our coasts, it also continues to diversify our water sources, digitalise its operations, and enhance water security.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The proposed amendments to the Public Utilities Act that I have elaborated on in my speech are necessary to ensure that the Public Utilities Act remains effective and relevant.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Singapore, being a small island nation surrounded by water, is vulnerable to rising sea levels.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, we must seriously take action to protect our country and our future generations as climate change is not a distant problem.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The establishment of the Coast and Flood Protection Fund is a concrete step in the right direction.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: It demonstrates the Government's commitment to make good judgement and give priority to Singapore’s long-term interests.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I know it is tempting for some political leaders to kick the can down the road, leaving it to the next government to handle.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Even amidst other challenges for budget, we must not be distracted from this crucial challenge.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Substantial funding is necessary to implement the coastal protection and drainage measures.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: What are the Government’s plans to ensure that there will be sufficient money in the Coastal and Flood Protection Fund?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: As I believe existing infrastructure will have to be enhanced, or even new infrastructure may have to be built as part of the protection measures, I hope we will tap on local resources and companies for these works?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, besides shoring up our coastal defences, we can also shore up our job creation for Singaporeans, and the local knowledge around such projects.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The low rainfall in Singapore and droughts affecting our neighbours such as Malaysia from whom we get our water supply give rise to grave concerns.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: There are different scenarios that can be played out: (a) reduce the supply of water to us; or (b) see the price of water going up.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The PUB has been doing a good job over the years to improve our self-sufficiency on water.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This means that a private organisation builds, owns and operates some of the facilities or structure of the plants, but there is some degree of support from the Government.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Together, these plants make up a significant part of our water supply.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I support this as water is our critical national resource.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We have to ensure that these DBOO plants are in good hands and operate reliably to meet our nation's water needs.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: However, given that PUB has been partnering with the private sector under the DBOO model for over 10 years, with majority of the partnerships being successful, some may wonder was the decision triggered by the situation with Hyflux?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Perhaps MCCY should also introduce this over our Sports Hub.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Nonetheless, the concession companies of these DBOO plants may be concerned about whether these powers will affect their rights and interests under their existing agreements with PUB.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister clarify when Special Administration Orders will be invoked, versus the existing contractual safeguards?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Even as our Government and Public services work tirelessly to develop our self-sufficiency and grow our water supply, we must not rest on our laurels, and we certainly cannot be complacent.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Every one of us residing in Singapore, from commercial entities and organisations to individuals, must play our part to use water responsibly.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Let us reduce, reuse and recycle water and do our part to mitigate the impact of climate change.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: (In Mandarin):   The Government has a long-term vision and plan to build more barrages along our coastlines.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This will not only help our local companies, but also ensure that we have enough relevant knowledge that will be useful in time of crises.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The Government also seeks to be empowered to issue Special Administration Orders to the water supply companies.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: However, it may also bring some uncertainties to relevant companies.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister clarify under what circumstances these powers will be invoked?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Everyone has a duty to save water to ensure that we have enough water resources.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, I applaud the decision to set up the Coastal and Flood Protection Fund.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In the face of climate change, we have not a moment to lose.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Our very survival depends on future-ready infrastructure and measures to kick start sustainable solutions.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Very fortunately, Singapore has had some money set aside for contingencies like this.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I really thank our predecessors from the bottom of my heart.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The battle against rising sea levels will be a long-drawn-out and expensive one.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In addition, the Fund must be ring-fenced and protected from the vagaries of domestic politics and economic cycles.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Would the Minister share what measures will be in place to ensure strict oversight and prudent utilisation of the Fund?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I expect that seawalls, land reclamation and planting of mangroves would be considered for different parts of our coast.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Due to our geographical constraints, we will have to cooperate with our immediate neighbouring countries for some of these coastal works for the benefit of all people.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Next, I welcome the relevant amendments and continual investments by both public and private sectors in our domestic water treatment capability.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, the question remains on the feasibility of the Design-Build-Own-Operate (DBOO) model.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In addition, will the Ministry be able to keep the facilities financially independent and operational while the operator is struggling to keep the company going, falling short of triggering the invocation of Special Administration Orders by the Minister or seeking redress by the high court?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Is the list of events of default sufficiently comprehensive?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Have they been reviewed to ensure that they are not overly rigid or restrictive in order for the Minister to invoke the orders when necessary?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With that, I conclude my support for the Bill.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I just want to make one comment that Er Dr Lee Bee Wah mentioned about self-sufficiency.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I think we have to be careful about this word.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We are not self-sufficient, but we should say we are resilient.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We are resilient against weather, we are resilient against possibly climate change just to put a point across.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I will begin by addressing coastal and flood protection issues first.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah and Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked for about the Government's plans to ensure that there are sufficient funds in the Coastal and Flood Protection Fund.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Climate change and rising sea levels will not only affect our current generation but future generations and beyond.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But once built, they benefit many generations of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This is a complex and significant, long-haul effort and we need to distribute the share of funding more equitably across current and future generations.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Setting up the Coastal and Flood Protection Fund now provides us with a longer runway to build up the Fund, and allows the Government to save up across successive terms.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The Government will top up the Fund whenever our fiscal situation allows.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: PUB is working with agencies to refine our modelling and develop more detailed plans on the type of protection measures required and the costs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This will allow the Government to better assess the funding required and financing options.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked what measures will be in place to ensure strict oversight and prudent utilisation of the Fund.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Second, PUB will have oversight over the management and withdrawal of the Fund.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Third like any other large scale and complex development projects the Government undertakes coastal protection and drainage measures will continue to be subject to MOF's evaluation and prevailing approval processes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked for some examples of the uses of the Fund.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Ensuring our flood resilience will require careful planning and seamless integration of protection measures in our infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: First, to prevent sea waters from flowing inland, we will need to construct structures such as sea walls, revetments, dykes, tide gates or barrages to serve as coastal defences and physical barriers.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will study the feasibility of all these options for our coastline.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Where feasible, we could even integrate nature-based solutions, such as the planting of mangroves to break wave energy.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: While structures such as tidal gates and barrages stop sea water from flowing inland, they would likewise prevent storm water from flowing out into the sea, especially when intense rainstorms coincide with high tides.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As such, we will need to install outlet pumps at some of our waterways to pump floodwaters into the sea.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah rightly pointed out the extent of infrastructure works required to protect our coastline.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: She asked if we will tap on local resources and companies in this journey.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Coastal protection is a new area in Singapore and capabilities will need to be built up.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will indeed have to tap on the best engineering capabilities available.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Where they are not available in Singapore, we will have to bring them in, even as we grow our own talent and capabilities.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The Government and industry will have to work hand in hand.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We are confident that over time, we will grow a strong and vibrant local industry, just like what we did with our water sector.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We hope that our local firms will proactively build up their capabilities in coastal protection, hydraulic modelling, and flood risk forecasting just to name a few areas, and to tap on these opportunities when available.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I will next address the questions on safeguards over PUB's DBOO plants.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked about the feasibility of the DBOO model and whether other operating models for water plants have been considered.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Besides the DBOO models, PUB also employs other models.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For example, PUB employs the design and build model where it partners the private sector to design and build the plants while PUB owns and operates the plants.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As explained in my opening speech. the DBOO model has been useful in allowing us to tap on private sector innovations and cost efficiencies to deliver water services more effectively.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: By combining design, build, own and operate functions in the same DBOO contract, it gives the private sector a strong incentive to ensure that the project design takes into consideration operational and other life-cycle costs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The DBOO model also strengthens the capacity of the private sector, just like Er Dr Lee Bee Wah has asked just now.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: When companies undertake DBOO projects, we hope they develop a track record that allows them to grow in our region and compete on the world stage.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked about PUB's ability to maintain oversight over concession companies which are struggling.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As I had explained in this House in April 2019, even though PUB does not interfere with business decisions made by the concession companies, PUB monitors the performance of the plants under the DBOO models to ensure that the concession companies can meet the contractual obligations to PUB.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Concession companies are required to submit financial reports to PUB on a regular basis.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Where there are issues, PUB will require the concession companies to rectify them, failing which, PUB may exercise its right to terminate the DBOO contracts and take control of the plants.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These contractual oversight will continue and, with the new legislative mechanism, will have greater assurance and oversight over our DBOO plants.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah rightly pointed out that PUB has been partnering with the private sector under DBOO model for over 10 years.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The majority of these partnerships have been successful.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Given this, why the decision to introduce legislative levers over DBOO plants now?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We concluded that it would be prudent to put in place similar safeguards, especially as more DBOO plants are being completed.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah also asked if the legislative levers over DBOO plants are triggered by the Hyflux situation.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: That said, the Hyflux situation was a reminder that we need to exercise proper oversight over our DBOO plants which are a key part of our water supply infrastructure and have effective levers to intervene when necessary in order to ensure Singapore's water security.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As mentioned in my opening speech, PUB has in place robust contractual safeguards which allowed us to successfully execute the contractual remedies for the Tuaspring Desalination Plant.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: With the additional legislative safeguards introduced under this Bill, we will further strengthen our oversight over critical water infrastructure and enhance our levers, in case it is necessary to intervene.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah and Mr Gan Thiam Poh also asked for elaboration on when and how Special Administration Orders will be invoked versus the existing contractual safeguards.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: PUB's interest is in safeguarding Singapore's water security.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These are similar to those found in a Special Administration Order regime of other essential services.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Such Orders are meant to ensure Singapore's water security and would be used only under exceptional circumstances.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I think of all the agencies that I have seen, PUB is one that has always maintained strong lines of engineers.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As old ones retire, new ones have learnt from them and they continue to give us the water security that we are comfortable with.
